{"basis":"measured","confidence":1.0,"fact_type":"observation","statement":"**ONE ROCKSDB STORE SERVES EVERY GIT BRANCH, SO THE LIVE GRAPH DOES NOT BRANCH — AND THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE IS A WORKFLOW RULE NOTHING STATES: YOU CANNOT HAVE TWO OPEN PULL REQUESTS THAT BOTH MAKE GRAPH WRITES.**

OBSERVED 2026-08-14 while holding PR #182 open (design-record writes) and being asked to build the command coverage accepted in it. `.reflow2/graph` is a single store shared by whatever branch is checked out; `git checkout <branch>` does not switch it. So any export taken on a second branch carries **the first branch's uncommitted graph writes too**, and both PRs then contain each other's nodes.

⇒ **THE CALL MADE, AND WHY:** the command-coverage build was FOLDED INTO #182 rather than opened as a third PR. **One PR at a time while graph writes are outstanding.** The alternative — branching from main and exporting — would have produced an export containing #182's nodes with a `prev_content_hash` pointing at main, i.e. a document silently claiming work that another open PR also claims. `rule:the-export-is-written-once-per-branch` and `dec:export-once-per-pr` constrain the export WITHIN a branch and say nothing about two branches sharing one store.

⚠️ **NOT MEASURED HERE:** the collision was avoided rather than reproduced. What is established is the mechanism (one store, no per-branch isolation) and the decision taken because of it — not an observed corrupted export. A deliberate reproduction would be cheap and has not been done.

═══ ⭐ THE SERVED-SURFACE GAP, WHICH IS THE PART THAT REACHES ANYONE ELSE ═══

**THE FIX ALREADY EXISTS AND IS SERVED — `parallel-work` sets up an isolated worktree with its own copy of the graph, which is exactly the isolation missing above. But the skill is framed by PEOPLE, not by BRANCHES:** *"Use when two or more people (or agents) need to work on one design at the same time without colliding — 'my brother and I are both editing this'."*

🛑 **ONE PERSON WITH TWO BRANCHES HITS THE IDENTICAL COLLISION AND WILL NOT REACH FOR A SKILL ABOUT COLLABORATING.** Every trigger phrase it lists is social; none is *"I have two PRs open"*. So the person most likely to hit this — a solo maintainer working two changes — is the one the skill's own trigger conditions exclude. That is AGENTS.md rule 7's shape: the lesson is real, and the served surface that would carry it does not currently invite the case.

📌 RELATED BUT DISTINCT, so this is not filed as a duplicate of any of them: `dec:multi-writer-architecture` covers the FILE as transport between people; `ver:merge-driver` covers merging the exported document; `rule:the-export-is-written-once-per-branch` and `fact:the-lineage-gate-verdict-depends-on-when-you-run-it` cover the chain WITHIN one branch. **None addresses two branches sharing one live store**, which is the only reason the fold-into-one-PR decision was needed.

⇒ OPEN, AND NOT PROPOSED AS A CHANGE HERE: whether `parallel-work`'s trigger conditions should name the solo-with-two-branches case, or whether something should notice that the store has writes belonging to a branch you are not on.
